headline: How human cells fix broken DNA
standfirst: Scientists have captured a rare look at how our bodies repair dangerous genetic damage.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: Researchers at Johns Hopkins University mapped how cells fix double-strand DNA breaks.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Two new scientific studies used advanced imaging to observe this complex repair process.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: These breaks are among the most dangerous types of genetic damage for our cells.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future research will likely build on these findings to better understand cell health.

caption:
Scientists at Johns Hopkins University have discovered how human cells repair DNA double strand breaks.

This research provides a new look at a vital process that keeps our genetic code intact. Understanding these emergency repairs could lead to better insights into how our bodies protect themselves from serious damage.
